messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — elevated 5xx rate observed on gateway-frontend (us-west-2). 5m window shows 5.9% 5xx, spike started ~3m ago. Top error: upstream timeouts (504) + some 502. Alerting channel and paging rotation.

sam (oncall): taking this. can someone confirm customer-facing impact?

eva (support): getting support tickets from two customers (search and auth flows) reporting intermittent timeouts and failed uploads. They see 502/504 in app logs.

sam (oncall): thanks. quick check: are traces coming through for these requests? I’m not seeing request IDs on a subset of gateway logs. looks like header strip/ingress rewrite happening.

marie: I'm seeing truncated X-Request-Id in gateway logs for ~40% of failed requests. traces for those ids are missing. sampling looks normal for other requests. may be a header size/regression.

carlos: infra note — we pushed a small envoy config change earlier today to tighten header bytes limits to avoid oversized header attacks. could be related if some clients send big cookies. rolling back envoy change would be quick if we confirm.

sam (oncall): good call. before rolling back, we should add stopgap instrumentation: 1) enable verbose request_id passthrough logs at edge for 10m, 2) bump trace sampling to 100% on gateway-frontend for 15m, 3) route a small % of traffic away from new envoys to old pool. any objections?

marie: +1. I can hotpatch logger and trace sampling. command:

```
# increase OTEL sampling via k8s patch
kubectl -n platform set env deploy/gateway-frontend OTEL_SAMPLING_RATE=1.0
# increase app log level for request-id passthrough
kubectl -n platform patch deploy gateway-edge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"log-level":"debug-temp"}}}}}'
```

carlos: I'll create a temporary traffic split in service mesh to move 20% traffic to the pre-change gateway variant:

```
# istio virtualservice patch (example)
kubectl -n platform patch virtualservice gateway --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/0/weight","value":80},{"op":"add","path":"/spec/http/0/route/1","value":{"destination":{"host":"gateway-prechange"},"weight":20}}]'
```

irene: I'm enabling 100% trace capture for gateway-frontend in datadog/otel. Will push a trace-forwarder rule so we don't lose spans even if request-id missing.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout/gateway-traffic-split started by carlos — 20% -> gateway-prechange. Status: in-progress.

sam (oncall): while those go, need quick evidence: marie, can you add a temp log forwarder for the edge debug logs to person-hours S3 (retention short) so we can search raw headers? If we find oversized headers, we can confirm the envoy change is culprit.

marie: doing that now. command I ran:

```
# temporary fluent-bit forward to s3 (30m retention via lifecycle)
kubectl -n logging apply -f fluent-bit-temp-forwarder.yaml
```

marie: added. also bumping JVM/gateway debug for request-parsing module.

carlos: traffic split in place. early telemetry: 5xx rate across whole fleet down from 5.9% -> 4.2% and gateway-prechange shows 0.8% 5xx. suggests the change is likely related.

sam (oncall): good signal. let's keep split for 30m while we dig. if logs show header truncation, we'll rollback envoy header limit change across the fleet.

eva (support): told impacted customers we are investigating, routing some traffic to a safer variant, and will update in 30 minutes.

irene: traces: found spans with no parent or request-id — many upstream components generate trace ids but the gateway was removing X-Request-Id header when it exceeded limit, creating orphan spans and losing correlations. attaching sample header dump (sanitized) below.

marie: found repeated cookie header lengths ~12KB for a small user-agent population. envoy header bytes limit was 8KB after the morning change. that matches.

sam (oncall): decision: rollback envoy header limit change. carlos, can you run rollback with a controlled rollout and keep 10% split until we observe stable 5xx < 1%? Post-rollback we keep trace capture and logs for 30 more minutes then revert debug levels.

carlos: rolling back envoy config now. command:

```
# rollback patch
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/envoy-proxy
# verify config
kubectl -n infra exec -it deploy/envoy-proxy -- curl localhost:9901/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.listener_name=="listener_0")'
```

deploy-bot: rollout/envoy-proxy rollback started by carlos — status: rolling.

carlos: rollback applied to 30% of pods so far. monitoring health.

sam (oncall): monitoring metrics: overall 5xx down to 1.1% and distinct customer error reports dropping. nice. keep split until we hit <1% for 2 consecutive 5m windows.

marie: confirming access to logs in s3, saved 420 header samples + trace dumps to s3://redwood-temp/edge-debug/2532109876/. will attach to postmortem.

irene: traces now re-associated for most requests. debug sampling captured the orphan spans which helped confirm the header truncation chain.

sam (oncall): assign postmortem owner: marie. scope: root cause (envoy header limit change), mitigation timeline, customer impact, and action items (pre-deploy traffic protection, test with large headers, add metric for header-drop counts).

marie: ack. I'll open postmortem and include mitigation checklist and follow-ups. first follow-up: add alert for header-trim events + increase default header limit or implement graceful handling.

carlos: done — envoy rollback completed fleetwide. 5xx steady at 0.4% now.

sam (oncall): great work all. I'll close the page after postmortem is filed and customers updated. leaving trace sampling/log-forwarders for another 20m then revert. thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary-rollout/gateway-traffic-split completed. rollout/envoy-proxy rollback completed.

sam (oncall): closing notes: two action items immediate — postmortem (marie), add header-drop metric (infra). anyone else?

marie: will add docs + test in staging for oversized headers.

eva (support): I'll send final customer update in 30m summarizing mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

sam (oncall): closing thread in 40m unless new regressions arise. thanks everyone.
